Apply dictionary mapping and standardize categorical values

Source: R/dict_apply.R
dict_apply.Rd

Renames variables and recodes factor labels to their numeric standard_code equivalents using the mapping sheets in the dictionary produced by dict_init(). Input data is sanitized via janitor::clean_names() before any processing.

Usage

dict_apply(data, wb_path, source_name, attributes = FALSE)

Arguments

data

A data.frame to be standardized.

wb_path

Character string. Path to the .xlsx dictionary file.

source_name

Character string. The column name in Variable_Map_Wide that corresponds to this dataset (e.g. "orig_wave1"). Must match the dictionary exactly.

attributes

Logical. If TRUE, the original variable names and descriptions from the dictionary are stored as attributes on the returned tibble. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

A tibble with variables renamed to their target_name and factor columns recoded to integer-level factors.

Examples

wave1 <- data.frame(id = c("alice", "bob"), gender = c("Female", "Male"))

dict_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
openxlsx::write.xlsx(
  list(
    Variable_Map_Wide = data.frame(
      target_name = c("id", "gender"),
      orig_w1     = c("id", "gender")
    ),
    Factor_Levels = data.frame(
      wave              = "orig_w1",
      original_variable = "gender",
      target_name       = "gender",
      original_level    = c("Female", "Male"),
      standard_code     = c(1, 2),
      standard_label    = c("Female", "Male")
    )
  ),
  file = dict_path
)

dict_apply(wave1, dict_path, source_name = "orig_w1")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   id    gender
#>   <chr> <fct> 
#> 1 alice 1     
#> 2 bob   2
